No public PolAir-specific threshold, control or fallback-capacity mechanism has been located that would prevent a growing observation/intervention imbalance if one exists.

Whether PolAir-Remote reduced dangerous vehicle pursuits - the one operational outcome in this section not already covered by AR-029/AR-030's undisclosed-outcome-measures findings - is likewise not established by any published aggregate Moree result.
mechanisms: Absence of published staffing, threshold and pursuit-outcome data is consistent with either the imbalance risk not materialising, or materialising without public disclosure; the public record does not distinguish these.
paths.boundary: No determination is made that a capacity imbalance has actually occurred, that staffing has not in fact increased through some unpublished channel, or that PolAir-Remote has or has not affected vehicle pursuits - only that the public record does not establish any of these, and that the mechanism by which an imbalance could occur is structurally plausible and currently unaddressed by any public control.

paths.title: Flight-Level Mission Data Schema and Disclosure Gap
analysis: Section E (Q128-Q149) of the Answer Register establishes that CASA's general operational-record baseline (referenced already by AR-019 for chain-of-custody purposes) does not resolve a distinct question: whether NSW Police's own mission-level dataset for PolAir-Remote assigns each flight a unique identifier, links it to an incident or event number, classifies it into a defined set of categories (reactive, proactive, training, testing, scheduled patrol, high-visibility operation, covert), and records what proportion of flights fall into each category. None of this classification structure, nor the geographic distribution data it would enable - areas of highest flight frequency, specific streets or neighbourhoods receiving repeated observation, areas of longest cumulative loiter time - is publicly disclosed.

A further, more granular layer is also undisclosed: whether flight-path geometry and altitude are retained beyond what the platform and CASA make technically possible, and whether sensor mode, zoom use, thermal use, recording status, operator identity, mid-flight purpose changes, and cross-flight tracking of the same person or vehicle across multiple separate missions are recorded and retained as distinct fields. This is a mission-data-schema gap, not a chain-of-custody gap: it concerns what NSW Police's own tasking and surveillance-footprint records contain, independent of whether any specific flight's imagery is later used as evidence.
determinations: NSW Police's own mission-level dataset structure - unique flight identifiers, incident linkage, and a defined flight-type classification with per-category proportions - is not publicly disclosed, beyond the general CASA record-keeping baseline AR-019 already established.
Geographic distribution data (areas of highest flight frequency, specific streets or neighbourhoods with repeated observation, areas of longest cumulative loiter time) is not publicly disclosed.

Granular per-flight technical fields (sensor mode, zoom, thermal use, recording status, operator identity, mid-flight purpose change, and cross-flight tracking of the same person or vehicle) are not confirmed as recorded or retained in the public record; flight-path and altitude retention are only partially established as technically possible, not confirmed as NSW Police's actual retention practice.
mechanisms: A general capability to log flights (CASA/platform) is publicly established; the specific schema NSW Police actually uses to classify and geographically aggregate PolAir-Remote flights is not.
paths.boundary: No determination is made about what NSW Police's actual internal mission-data schema contains; only that its structure and content are not publicly disclosed at the level of detail this section's questions specify.

paths.title: Flight-Geography Demographic and Spatial Disproportionality Analysis Gap
analysis: Section E (Q150-Q158) of the Answer Register establishes that joining flight geography against Aboriginal population distribution, offence location, socioeconomic disadvantage, and proactive-policing operations is technically feasible in principle - if a de-identified flight-geography dataset were released, it could be joined to already-public demographic, offence and spatial datasets - but NSW Police has not published that flight-geography dataset, so no such join has been performed by anyone outside the organisation.

Absent that dataset, none of this section's specific analytical questions - whether some communities are exposed to more aerial observation than their offence incidence would predict, whether private residential areas are disproportionately represented in flight paths, whether repeated patrol routes or predictable patrol times exist, and whether geographic or temporal displacement of activity has been assessed - can currently be answered from the public record. This is distinct from AR-015's consultation-sequencing finding (which concerns whether communities had input before deployment) and AR-012's biometric/AI-governance gap (which concerns identification technology): this path concerns whether the surveillance footprint itself, independent of any identification capability or consultation process, is disclosed and analysable for disproportionate spatial impact.
determinations: Joining flight geography against demographic and spatial datasets (Aboriginal population distribution, offence location, socioeconomic disadvantage, proactive-policing operations) is technically feasible in principle but has not been performed, because NSW Police has not published the underlying de-identified flight-geography dataset.

Whether any community is exposed to aerial observation disproportionate to its offence incidence, and whether private residential areas are disproportionately represented in flight paths, cannot currently be determined from the public record.

Whether flight patrol routes and times are repeated or predictable, and whether geographic or temporal displacement of activity has occurred, are open analytical questions requiring data not currently public.
mechanisms: The absence of a released flight-geography dataset prevents any independent disproportionality analysis; this does not establish that disproportionate exposure exists, only that it cannot currently be tested.
paths.boundary: No determination is made that flight patterns are or are not geographically or demographically disproportionate; only that the public record does not currently contain what would be needed to test this either way.

paths.title: Secondary-Detection Purpose-Change Authorization and Audit-Trail Gap
analysis: Section F (Q159-Q165, Q177) of the Answer Register addresses what happens the moment a PolAir-Remote mission tasked for one incident observes an unrelated possible offence. General policing law permits a new police event to be generated from lawfully obtained information, and legal-authority requirements for further action are fact-dependent rather than fixed - so neither of those general propositions is in dispute. What is not established is the PolAir-Remote-specific decision process itself: who authorises a mid-mission change of observation purpose, whether the operator must document the secondary purpose, whether a separate tasking record is created, and whether the same rule applies to live observation as to footage retained afterward.

This is a distinct governance layer from AR-010's reactive/proactive operating-mode contradiction, which concerns which overall mode the program uses, and from AR-019's evidence-handling/chain-of-custody gap, which concerns imagery once it is already being treated as courtroom evidence: this path concerns the internal decision moment at which a single mission's own scope expands, before any evidentiary or courtroom question arises. Q177's mandatory-audit-trail question is the most consequential of the eight items here, because its absence would mean the moment a mission's purpose changes is not necessarily independently reconstructable from any record at all.
determinations: No public PolAir-Remote-specific rule establishes who authorises a mid-mission change of observation purpose, or on what basis.
No public rule confirms mandatory documentation of a secondary purpose, a separate tasking record, or a distinct audit-trail requirement for purpose changes.
Whether the same authorization/documentation rule applies to live observation as to footage retained afterward is not established.

This gap concerns the internal decision process at the moment of purpose change, distinct from AR-019's evidentiary chain-of-custody gap (imagery already treated as courtroom evidence) and AR-010's operating-mode contradiction (the program's overall stated mode).
mechanisms: The absence of a public authorization/audit-trail rule for purpose changes is consistent with an internal rule existing but not being published, or with no such rule existing at all; the public record does not distinguish these.
paths.boundary: No determination is made that any purpose change has occurred without authorization or documentation in practice; only that no public rule establishes what that authorization or documentation requirement is.

paths.title: Downstream Legal-Escalation and Secondary-Detection Reporting Gap
analysis: The remaining thirteen items in Section F (Q166-Q176, Q178-Q179) concern what an incidental or secondary detection can lead to once it occurs. No public PolAir-Remote-specific rule or threshold establishes whether such a detection alone can justify a search, a pursuit, an arrest, or the creation of an intelligence record; whether incidental imagery can be retained after the originating mission ends, searched retrospectively for an unrelated investigation, or reused for another purpose without a fresh approval; or whether an unrelated person or vehicle observed only incidentally can be tracked, or thermal imaging and AI-assisted tracking activated once the mission's purpose has changed.

AR-020 already established that NSW law provides real, if circumstance-dependent, secondary-use pathways for law-enforcement information generally (PPIP Act s 23); this path is narrower and more operational - it asks whether PolAir-Remote specifically has a published threshold or process governing when an incidental detection converts into one of these further actions, and finds none. The final two items (Q178-Q179) compound the gap: secondary detections are not confirmed as tracked as a distinct operational category at all, so even the frequency with which incidental observation leads to further police action is unknown from the public record - there is no visible starting point from which to measure how often this pathway is actually used.
determinations: No public PolAir-Remote-specific threshold or process establishes whether an incidental/secondary detection alone can justify a search, pursuit, arrest, or intelligence record.

No public rule establishes whether incidental imagery can be retained past the originating mission, searched retrospectively for an unrelated investigation, or reused for another purpose without fresh approval.

No public rule establishes whether an unrelated person or vehicle observed incidentally can be tracked, or whether thermal imaging or AI-assisted tracking can be activated once a mission's purpose has changed.

Secondary detections are not confirmed as recorded or reported as a distinct operational category, so the frequency with which incidental observation leads to further police action is not established from the public record.
mechanisms: PPIP Act s 23 establishes that a legal pathway for this kind of secondary use exists in principle (AR-020); whether PolAir-Remote's own practice actually applies a defined threshold or process for it, or how often, is not publicly reconstructable.
paths.boundary: No determination is made that any incidental detection has in fact been used to justify a search, arrest, or tracking action, or that any of these have occurred without proper authority; only that no public threshold, process, or frequency data exists to test this.

paths.title: Private-Property Aerial Observation Boundary Is Not Publicly Defined
analysis: Section G (Q180-Q189) of the Answer Register puts ten specific, distinct questions to the public record about where the boundary of PolAir-Remote's permitted aerial observation of private property sits: yards, home exteriors, windows, deliberate viewing through windows, zoom into residential property, thermal observation of homes, prolonged loitering over residences, altitude or angle restrictions, and whether any of the foregoing differs between emergency response and proactive patrol, or when a person is suspected of an offence. Every one of the ten receives materially the same answer: no NSW Police PolAir-Remote-specific operational rule addressing that dimension has been publicly located, and general law is not shown to substitute for the missing police-specific limit.

This is a distinct governance layer from AR-012's AI/biometric-processing gap, which concerns what may be done with imagery once captured, and from AR-010's reactive/proactive operating-mode contradiction, which concerns which overall mode the program is described as using: this path concerns the prior question of where and how imagery of private property may be captured in the first place. Q188 asks directly whether the undisclosed boundary itself varies by operating mode, and Q189 whether it varies when a person is suspected of an offence - meaning even the conditions under which the boundary might shift are themselves undocumented, not only the boundary's substantive content.
determinations: No public PolAir-Remote-specific rule addresses any of ten distinct private-property observation-boundary dimensions tested: yards, home exteriors, windows, deliberate window viewing, zoom, thermal observation, loitering, altitude/angle, an emergency-versus-proactive-patrol distinction, or a suspected-offence distinction.
General law is not shown to substitute for the missing PolAir-Remote-specific limit on any of these ten dimensions.

Whether an undisclosed boundary, if one exists internally, varies between emergency response and proactive patrol, or when a person is suspected of an offence, is itself not established from the public record.
mechanisms: The materially identical answer recorded against all ten items is consistent with a single templated non-answer rather than ten independently-resolved negatives; the public record does not distinguish an unpublished internal rule from the absence of any rule at all.
paths.boundary: No determination is made about NSW Police's actual internal practice on any of these ten dimensions, or that any specific flight has observed private property in a manner that would breach an undocumented boundary; only that no public rule establishes where that boundary sits.

paths.title: Warrant-Authority Ambiguity and Absent Privacy-Incident/Complaint Architecture
analysis: The remaining nine items in Section G (Q190-Q198) shift from where the observation boundary sits (AR-042) to what governs crossing it and what happens afterward. Three items (Q190-Q192) establish that the applicable legal-authority and warrant-requirement questions are fact-specific rather than settled by any single public rule: the Surveillance Devices Act does not establish a blanket rule that every drone view of private property needs a warrant, and what other warrant or authority might be required depends on the operation type and the applicable police power, neither of which is specified in the abstract. The remaining six items (Q193-Q198) establish that no public PolAir-Remote-specific document names who advises operators approaching this boundary or what process exists if it is breached, accidentally or deliberately - and that whether privacy incidents are even logged as a distinct category, and how many complaints have been made or substantiated, are not established from the public record.

AR-016 already established that NSW's formal complaint architecture (principally the LECC) has clear, systemic jurisdiction over PolAir-Remote governance concerns, and that the practical accountability gap is a resident's inability to discover whether a specific flight occurred, not the absence of a complaint mechanism itself. Section G sharpens that finding one layer further: even setting the discoverability problem aside, no public record establishes that an internal escalation route or incident-logging process exists at all for the specific case of a suspected private-property observation-boundary breach, or that complaint volume or substantiation data for this category is tracked anywhere. A resident who does learn a flight occurred would still have no visible internal process shown to receive that concern, nor any published figure showing the mechanism has ever been used for this purpose.
determinations: No single public rule establishes a blanket legal authority or blanket warrant requirement for drone observation of private activity; both are stated to be fact-specific, and no public criteria establish how that fact-specific determination is to be made.
No public PolAir-Remote-specific document identifies an operational or legal adviser, or an escalation route, for private-property observation-boundary questions.
No public PolAir-Remote-specific process establishes what occurs following an accidental or deliberate observation-boundary breach.

Whether privacy incidents are logged as a distinct operational category, and the number of privacy complaints made or substantiated, are not established from the public record - extending AR-016's discoverability finding to the internal incident-tracking layer itself.
mechanisms: AR-016 established that a resident cannot discover whether a specific flight occurred; this section shows the internal incident-logging and complaint-count layer is not established as existing either, which would remain a barrier even if individual-flight discoverability were resolved.
paths.boundary: No determination is made that any observation-boundary breach has occurred, that any complaint has been filed, or that any complaint-handling failure has taken place; only that no public rule establishes the applicable warrant/authority test in specific terms, or confirms the existence of an incident-logging and complaint-count architecture for this category.

cross_path_observations.title: Real capability, real problem, unverified specific claims
cross_path_observations.analysis: PolAir-Remote's tactical utility and Kempsey's community-safety concern are both independently documented (AR-004, AR-009); every specific quantitative claim built on top of them in the petition is separately unverified (AR-003, AR-004, AR-005, AR-007). These are not the same finding and must not be conflated.

cross_path_observations.title: Expansion planning predates the petition on every axis checked
cross_path_observations.analysis: Statewide RPAS procurement (AR-013), a second Aviation Command operating-model review (AR-013), and public contemplation of Kempsey as an expansion site (AR-002) all predate the August 2026 petition. The petition amplifies an institutional trajectory rather than originating it.

cross_path_observations.title: Two contradictions share one root cause: undisclosed operational policy
cross_path_observations.analysis: Both the reactive/proactive messaging contradiction (AR-010) and the crime-only/multi-purpose contradiction (AR-011) would be resolved by the same missing document: the controlling RPAS operational policy sought in GIPA Application 2.

cross_path_observations.title: Continuation, procurement, and absent exit criteria form one pattern, not three
cross_path_observations.analysis: Operating past the stated six-month window (AR-014), parallel enterprise procurement (AR-013), and the absence of any public stop/decommissioning criteria (AR-014, AR-016) read separately as three minor gaps; read together they describe a single institutional trajectory with no visible off-ramp.

cross_path_observations.title: Governance documentation gaps recur across every domain examined
cross_path_observations.analysis: No controlling operational policy (AR-010), no AI Assessment Framework determination (AR-012), no chain-of-custody protocol (AR-019), no child/Indigenous-specific data governance document (AR-020), and no stop/decommissioning criteria (AR-014) are five separate instances of the same structural pattern: operational capability that has outpaced its own public governance documentation.

cross_path_observations.title: GIPA is the common resolution path for almost every open question
cross_path_observations.analysis: Of the 18 open questions in this case's register, all but two (Q-0008, the Macleay Argus article; Q-0009, formal parliamentary petition status) resolve through one of the six already-drafted GIPA applications (AR-021). This case's evidentiary gaps are unusually concentrated on a single, already-identified acquisition mechanism.

cross_path_observations.title: Accountability exists in principle but requires the resident to already know a flight occurred
cross_path_observations.analysis: LECC has real, systemic complaint jurisdiction (AR-016) and NSW law provides real GIPA access (AR-021), but neither can be triggered by a resident who has no way to learn a specific drone flight occurred over their property - the practical accountability gap is discoverability, not the absence of a formal route.

cross_path_observations.title: Economic claims omit the same downstream chain in two different domains
cross_path_observations.analysis: The petition's cost claim omits downstream justice-system costs that a drone-driven arrest can trigger (AR-005, AR-018) in the same way its crime-reduction claim omits the confounding effect of bail-law and diversion programs on the same offender cohort (AR-006, AR-008) - both are instances of a single-input claim ignoring a documented downstream system.

cross_path_observations.title: Consultation and community-governance sequencing repeats the Moree pattern risk
cross_path_observations.analysis: Public consultation followed deployment at Moree (AR-015) in the same way public claims preceded verification throughout this case (AR-003 through AR-005) - a recurring pattern of public-facing process occurring after, rather than before, the substantive decision or claim it is nominally testing.

cross_path_observations.title: Baseline convergence: a real capability seeking expansion faster than its own evidentiary and governance base can support it
cross_path_observations.analysis: Across independent paths, PolAir-Remote is a real, tactically useful capability inside an active statewide expansion trajectory whose specific public justifications (crime statistics, cost, deployment speed) and governance documentation (operational policy, AI assessment, exit criteria, chain of custody) have not caught up with the pace of that trajectory.

cross_path_observations.title: Five mechanisms, one headline number, and a second unmeasured layer on top of it
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-023's incapacitation/displacement/substitution alternatives and AR-024's deterrence-signalling alternative extend AR-006's counterfactual-design gap into the specific mechanisms it contains: at least five distinct, non-exclusive mechanisms (incapacitation, geographic displacement, temporal displacement, offence substitution, deterrence) could each independently produce Moree's headline youth-crime decline, and none has been measured, ruled out, or disentangled from the others in the public record. AR-025 separately establishes that the political narrative built on top of that same headline number tracks visible activity (arrests, rallies, publicised recoveries) rather than the underlying outcome measures (prevented offences, desistance, perceived safety) any of these five mechanisms would actually require to evaluate. Read together, the petition's central causal claim and the political urgency built on top of it both rest on unmeasured layers, not one.

cross_path_observations.title: Total evaluation opacity across all 47 checked dimensions of the Moree trial's own assessment process
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-026 through AR-031 independently checked every dimension of the Moree trial's evaluation apparatus identified by the case's own Continuing Investigation Question Bank - existence, authorship, independence and methodology (AR-026); pre-deployment success/failure/continuation/expansion/termination criteria (AR-027); baseline, comparison and confounder-treatment design (AR-028); nine operational outcome measures (AR-029); nine rights- and equity-facing outcome measures (AR-030); and publication commitment plus the decision it is meant to control (AR-031) - and found the same undisclosed status on all 47 questions checked (Q1-Q47), not a sample of them. This is distinct from CPO-005's separate finding that governance-documentation gaps recur across different policy domains (operational policy, AI assessment, chain of custody, child/Indigenous data governance, exit criteria): this observation is about the completeness of the gap within a single trial's own evaluation process specifically, checked question-by-question rather than domain-by-domain, and it is a stronger structural finding than any of AR-026 through AR-031 read alone - there is currently no publicly disclosed dimension of the Moree evaluation on which this investigation could test a scaling decision against.

cross_path_observations.title: No official measurement and no independent data pathway either, for equity-facing surveillance impact
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-030 already established that no public results table shows whether the Moree trial's own evaluation measured demographic impact or Aboriginal justice-system contact as trial outcomes. AR-038 and AR-039 now establish that this gap is not merely an evaluation-design omission NSW Police could in principle fix by publishing its existing evaluation: the underlying mission-level flight dataset that would let anyone outside the organisation independently test geographic or demographic disproportionality - who is observed, how often, and where - is itself neither structured for that purpose in any publicly disclosed way (AR-038) nor released in de-identified form (AR-039). Read together, there is currently no channel, official or independent, through which this investigation or any outside party could test whether PolAir-Remote's surveillance footprint falls disproportionately on any community.

cross_path_observations.title: The secondary-detection gap is where AR-020's abstract legal pathway and AR-012's undisclosed AI-governance status meet at one live operational moment
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-020 established that NSW law provides real, if circumstance-dependent, secondary-use legal pathways for law-enforcement information in the abstract (PPIP Act s 23), and AR-012 established that no public AI Assessment Framework determination exists for PolAir-Remote despite a mandatory governance pathway existing in principle. AR-040 and AR-041 now show these two abstract gaps converge at one concrete, recurring operational moment: when a PolAir-Remote mission incidentally observes something outside its original purpose, no public rule establishes who may authorise pursuing it, document it, or activate AI-assisted tracking for it, nor how often this actually happens. The legal capacity and the technology both plainly exist; the specific policy and audit trail governing this exact junction between them do not appear to be publicly documented.

contradictions_preserved.issue: Reactive/"not surveillance" framing versus proactive and covert flying at trial commencement
contradictions_preserved.analysis: NSW Police's 19 February 2026 formal-launch messaging and the 8 January 2026 trial-commencement briefing describe materially different operating modes for the same program; resolution requires the controlling operational policy.

contradictions_preserved.issue: "Solely used for crime" versus documented multi-purpose emergency use
contradictions_preserved.analysis: A June 2026 quote describing crime-only use is in tension with January 2026 and other reporting describing search-and-rescue, motor-vehicle-collision and fire response uses; neither statement is shown false, but public framing is inconsistent.

overreach_controls: No determination that any specific numeric claim in the petition (50%, 100+, 70+, six, 30-60 seconds, helicopter-cost-fraction) is false - only that none is currently independently reproducible from a primary published dataset.
No determination that PolAir-Remote has had no effect, or a positive effect, on Moree crime - the causal question remains genuinely open on the public record.
No determination that facial recognition or biometric matching is currently occurring - the public record cannot establish this either way.
No determination that NSW Police predetermined the Moree trial outcome, unlawfully extended it, or committed to any specific Mid North Coast rollout.
No determination that consultation with Moree or any community was conducted in bad faith.
No determination that PolAir-Remote evidence has been mishandled in any actual criminal proceeding.
No determination that any child's or Aboriginal person's data has been mishandled by this program specifically.
No attribution of intent, bad faith, corruption or negligence to any named individual or institution.
No inference that a public-record absence proves an internal record, policy or control does not exist.
No forward projection, event-horizon statement, or Temporal Projection Integrity Engine classification - see that stage separately.
No Lattice Atlas topology claim or cross-thread structural declaration - see that stage separately.
No compression of PolAir-Remote's genuine, independently-documented tactical successes into an overall negative assessment of the technology.
